To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DFT primitive can be used as the basis of efficient parallel optical-computing algorithms for a wide range of problems and, in many cases, these algorithms are asymptotically optimal.

the DFT-VL-SIO model is an excellent model for optical computing, that the DFT circuit model captures some of the unique features of optical computing, and that the paradigms developed in this thesis provide a powerful methodology for developing parallel algorithms for optical-computing applications.

the DFT-VLIO model is a very useful tool for developing fast optical-computing algorithms and that the DFT-circuits model is a very good tool for developing algorithms that can be implemented with optical circuits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient parallel algorithms for optical-computing models.
the design and analysis of efficient parallel algorithms in the DFT-VL-SIO and DFT-circuit models.
the design and analysis of parallel algorithms for the optical computer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the parallel-algorithm designer has to work harder to achieve the same performance in the VLSIO model that is achieved in the random-access machine model by using the standard parallel-algorithm techniques.
, for the problems considered here, the VLSIO model is a good model of optical computing.
the optical-computers are very fast but have limited memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with the exception of a few problems, optical computing is at most polylogarithmically faster than the random-access machine model of computation.
we have developed efficient parallel algorithms for a variety of problems on a model that captures many of the characteristics of optical computing.
, for a large class of problems, the DFT-circuits model is a good abstraction of optical computing, and the VLSIO model is a good model for VLSI computing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
optical-computing technology has the potential to solve a wide range of problems in parallel computing.
the DFT-VSIO and the DFT-Circuit models are good models of optical computing and that the DFT can be used to develop efficient parallel algorithms in these optical-computing models.
optical-computing algorithms can often be derived by using standard parallel-algorithm design techniques.
